title: SandpaneCoreCapabilities
description: system.probe result: protocol version + capability discovery. Capabilities come from known tested commands, documented minimum versions, and actual runtime verification — never optimistic guesses (specs/08 §3).

instanceId.description: Unique per running Core instance; changes across restarts so clients can detect them.

verified.description: True ONLY after the adapter passed its in-SBX feasibility gate (P0).

supportsResume.description: Native-session resume advertised ONLY after restart tests pass.

methods.description: Feature discovery: the dotted wire names of EVERY method this Core actually dispatches, derived from sandpane_protocol::Method::ALL (never a hand-written list). Clients use it to detect optional methods (task.list, conversation.list, conversation.history) instead of assuming them from a version number. Absent only from a pre-discovery v1 Core, so it is not required here (additive); every current Core emits it.

features.description: Optional protocol features this Core implements (A2, additive), derived from the single list sandpane_protocol::FEATURES. A feature names behaviour a client cannot infer from `methods` (a pre-A2 Core silently drops an unknown request field): 'idempotency-keys' (sandbox.create / conversation.send honour idempotencyKey), 'sandbox-create-agent' (sandbox.create honours agent), 'conversation-sandbox-id' (A3b: conversation.create persists sandboxId and every Conversation carries it when one was stored; without it a client cannot tell 'no sandbox chosen' from 'an older Core discarded it'), 'conversation-send-mode' (A4: conversation.send honours mode "task" | "discuss" — any other string is VALIDATION_FAILED. Every TaskSummary created from A4 on carries mode (the send mode, an open string). It carries chosenSandboxName only when its chat chose a sandbox: a stored NAME, not a binding, and it never means the task runs in that sandbox; sandboxName keeps its pre-A4 binding-only meaning. A client must send mode only when this is advertised, because a pre-A4 Core silently drops it and would treat a discussion as a task), 'git-apply' (A6: git.apply applies reviewed host_worktree entries — git.review answers carry reviewId, hostHooksPath and per-entry taskBlob/taskMode, git.diff carries taskBlob/taskMode, git.apply takes reviewId + entries copied verbatim from that review and answers appliedFiles/modeChanges/snapshotTree/partial; without it a client keeps Apply in its 'not implemented' state). Deliberately NOT an enum: clients must ignore feature strings they do not know. `items.examples` lists the features this protocol revision defines and is the value set the drift gate compares. Absent from a pre-A2 Core = nothing advertised.
